Tenders closed 24/08/2026 via the Hungarian EKR e-procurement system; the sole award criterion is the total NET (excl. VAT) offer price in HUF. NO estimated value is published on the notice. The distinction matters commercially: nShield is a general-purpose key-storage HSM, payShield is a PAYMENT HSM (PIN translation, card-key management, remote key injection). Printec's opening at MNB is the payments-HSM and PCI-PIN layer, not general key storage.
signals.likelihood: Award within 1-3 months; Entrust/its Hungarian reseller near-certain given the branded spec

signals.signal: STRUCTURAL FINDING, stated with what was searched. Across 219 cached in-scope TED notices (13/07/2026-27/08/2026, CPV 30123000/30144400/30142000/35120000/50310000/50312000, ten countries) PLUS my own TED Search API v3 queries on CPV 30123400/30123600/30123610/30123620/30123630/30124000/30131000/30132000/30132200/30144200/30144400/30162000/42994000/66110000/66172000, on the title terms bankomat, Geldautomat, bankovky/bankovek, and on the named buyers Banka Slovenije, Banka Nationala a Romaniei, Česká národní banka, Magyar Nemzeti Bank, Národná banka Slovenska, Hrvatska narodna banka, Българска народна банка, Central Bank of Cyprus, Münze Österreich, Geldservice Austria, Česká pošta, Slovenská pošta, Hrvatska pošta, Pošta Slovenije and Poșta Română — there is exactly ONE ATM-classified (CPV 30123200) procurement in the whole EU footprint: the unawarded Geldservice Austria EUR 9.1m recycler framework. Every other cash-technology notice sits at a CENTRAL BANK, a MINT, a POST or a STATE FINANCIAL AGENCY. No commercial bank in GRC/ROU/BGR/HRV/SVN/CZE/SVK/HUN/CYP/AUT published an ATM, recycler, TCR or POS tender on TED in this window.
signals.implies: This is a finding, not a gap. Commercial banks in these ten markets are private-sector buyers not bound by the EU procurement directives, so their ATM/recycler/POS spend NEVER reaches TED. TED is therefore the right instrument for exactly four Printec buyer types — central banks (banknote sorters, HSMs, physical security), mints (coin handling), posts (counters, wrapping, packaging, technical protection) and state financial agencies (coin counters, cashier outsourcing) — and the wrong instrument for the bank ATM fleet. The bank pipeline has to come from Prozorro (UA), national portals, and direct account coverage.
signals.likelihood: Structural; will not change
signals.followup: Keep the TED sweep scoped to central banks / mints / posts / state financial agencies + the CPV 30123200 tripwire for any rare bank filing; do not treat TED silence on bank ATMs as market softness.

access_issues: No blocks encountered. TED Search API v3 (POST https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search) answered every query without authentication. All notice XMLs were fetched from https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/<id>/xml with a desktop Chrome User-Agent header and returned full eForms UBL. ONE partial failure and its fallback: https://ted.europa.eu/en/notice/511411-2026/xml (Magyar Nemzeti Bank HSM tender) returned an empty/unparseable body on the EN route; I retried the SAME notice on the Hungarian language route https://ted.europa.eu/hu/notice/511411-2026/xml with the same desktop User-Agent and got the full 37.5 KB XML, which is where the nShield 5c mid specification, the 36-month support term and the 24/08/2026 deadline come from. Worth recording as a general technique: when a TED notice XML comes back empty on /en/, retry on the filing language path. The TED API's notice-title~ operator performs fuzzy multilingual expansion and returned large volumes of irrelevant historic notices (e.g. a 'bankovky' query surfaced 2016-2017 Belgian and French banknote-printing notices); I therefore treated title queries as a discovery aid only and confirmed every kept result against its own XML. Buyer-name and CPV queries were reliable. No CAPTCHA was encountered and none was attempted; no login wall was worked around.
operator_requests: none — every source needed this run was reachable without gating, payment or login. All figures come from openly published eForms XML.
